pl-l4d25c1-d1e115.summary: Asks whether heretics cut off and condemned by the Church can confer holy orders, and whether those ordained by them must be reordained on returning to the Church's unity.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e118.summary: Notes that the doctors' words, which seem to disagree greatly, make this question complex and almost insoluble.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e121.summary: Reports that some seem to teach that heretics cannot give holy orders, and those seemingly ordained by them receive no grace.
claims: Some hold heretics cannot confer orders.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e125.summary: Gives Innocent: Arian clerics should not be received with the dignity of priesthood or ministry, only their Trinitarian baptism being valid; they cannot give the Spirit they lost; those ordained by heretics have a wounded head; one who lost honor cannot give it, nor did the recipient receive anything; those coming from heretics should be given lay communion by laying on of hands and not promoted to clerical rank.
claims: Innocent denies validity to heretical ordinations.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e146.summary: Gives Gregory: the Arians' consecration is sacrilegious when communion is received from their hand.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e152.summary: Gives Cyprian: all that heretics do is carnal, empty, and sacrilegious; their altars false, their priesthoods and sacrifices sacrilegious; like apes imitating men they claim the Church's face and authority while outside it; no offering can be sacrificed where the Spirit is not, nor do the prayers of one who violated God help anyone.
claims: Cyprian holds heretical sacraments empty and sacrilegious.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e161.summary: Gives Jerome: all heretics offer is contaminated before the Lord; though seemingly holy in form, touched by the polluted, all is polluted.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e170.summary: Adds Jerome: God hates and casts away heretics' sacrifices and closes his nostrils at their stench whenever they gather in his name.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e176.summary: Adds Jerome: they offer sacrilegious bread.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e183.summary: Gives Leo: outside the Church neither priesthoods are valid nor sacrifices true.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e189.summary: Adds Leo: through cruel madness the light of all sacraments was extinguished in the see of Alexandria; the offering of sacrifice ceased, the sanctification of chrism failed, and all mysteries withdrew from the impious' parricidal hands.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e195.summary: Draws out that these texts seem to establish that the Church's sacraments, especially the body and blood, ordination, and confirmation, cannot be ministered by heretics.
claims: Some authorities deny heretics can minister the eucharist, orders, and confirmation.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e198.summary: Reports others who hold that holy orders, like baptism, can be given even by separated heretics, and those ordained and baptized there need not be reordained or rebaptized on returning.
claims: Others hold heretical ordination valid and unrepeatable.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e201.summary: Quotes Augustine: the claim that one who leaves the Church keeps baptism but loses the right to give it is vain, since no reason shows why one who cannot lose baptism could lose the right to give it; both are sacraments given by consecration, at baptism and ordination, so neither may be repeated. Leaders returning from schism, if allowed to keep their offices, are not reordained; their ordination remained whole, the fault being in the separation, corrected by unity, not in the sacraments. If it seems better that they not exercise office, the sacrament is not taken from them nor hands laid on them again, lest the sacrament be wronged. As there is something in baptism they can give, so in ordination there is the right to give; to have is different from having harmfully or salutarily.
claims: Ordination, like baptism, remains and is not repeated.
The fault is in separation, not in the sacrament.
One can have a sacrament harmfully or salutarily.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e213.summary: Adds Augustine: there is no question that those separated from unity have and can give the sacraments, but harmfully, being outside the bond of peace; neither sacrament must be wronged; as one who leaves unity has but not rightly, and so it is not restored on return, so he gives but not rightly, and the recipient is not re-given it on coming to unity.
claims: Separated persons have and give sacraments, though harmfully.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e223.summary: Adds Augustine: not having something differs from not having it rightly or usurping it unlawfully; the sacraments do not cease to be Christ's and the Church's because heretics and the impious use them unlawfully; the users are to be corrected and punished, the sacraments acknowledged and revered.
claims: Unlawful use does not make the sacraments cease to be Christ's.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e229.summary: Gives Gregory: the suggestion that those ordained be ordained again is ridiculous; as one baptized once must not be rebaptized, so one consecrated once cannot be consecrated again in the same order.
claims: Ordination, like baptism, cannot be repeated.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e238.summary: Draws out that these texts seem to assert that Christ's sacraments remain with the right of giving in all the impious, even condemned heretics; they can give, though harmfully, and those they ordain are not reordained; which seems opposed to the earlier authorities.
claims: These authorities affirm that heretics retain and can confer sacraments.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e241.summary: Reports one resolution: heretics who received priestly or episcopal anointing and left the Church keep the right of baptizing but lack the power of conferring holy orders or consecrating the Lord's body after being cut off and condemned by the Church, as a degraded bishop cannot confer orders but can still baptize.
claims: On one view, condemned heretics lose the power to ordain and consecrate but not to baptize.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e244.summary: Continues this resolution: Augustine's words concern heretics separated from truth and unity by their own perverse sense, not yet by the Church's sentence, who keep the right to consecrate and ordain; those they ordain before manifest separation need not be reordained even if they later left and were condemned. Texts allowing those ordained by heretics to minister refer to such cases; after cutting off and condemnation, the right is removed, as from the degraded or excommunicated.
claims: Augustine's texts concern heretics not yet condemned by the Church.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e250.summary: Reports a second resolution: sacraments celebrated by separated heretics in the Church's form are true and valid, since they did not lose the right to give and consecrate, and those so ordained are not reordained; but what heretics do otherwise than the Church is false and void, and those so ordained receive a wound, not a gift; the doctors speak variously according to this difference.
claims: Heretical sacraments in the Church's form are valid; in another form, void.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e254.summary: Reports a third resolution: separated heretics can celebrate the same sacraments as Catholics if they keep the Church's form; these are true and valid in themselves but false and void in effect for those who handle and receive them badly, since they do not give what they promise; they are called damnable and polluted not in themselves but because of unworthy handling, as Gregory calls Arian communion execration, Innocent calls Bonosus's ordination damnation, and Jerome calls their sacrifices bread of mourning, with respect to effect.
claims: Heretical sacraments are valid in themselves but void in effect.
Condemnatory language refers to effect, not essence.

pl-l4d25c1-d1e263.summary: Reports a fourth view: heretics ordained within the Church keep the right to ordain and consecrate even when separated, but those ordained and anointed by them while in schism or heresy lack it, so when they try to ordain they inflict a wound rather than confer grace.
claims: On another view, only those ordained within the Church keep the power to ordain.

pl-l4d25c1.summary: Asks whether heretics cut off and condemned by the Church can confer holy orders, and whether those they ordain must be reordained on returning. The doctors seem to disagree sharply. Innocent, Gregory, Cyprian, Jerome, and Leo seem to say heretics cannot give orders or the Spirit, that their consecrations and sacrifices are sacrilegious and void. Augustine and Gregory say the opposite: as baptism is not lost or repeated, neither is the right to ordain; heretics have and give the sacraments, though to their ruin, and those ordained by them are not reordained. Lombard reports several resolutions: that heretics condemned by the Church lose the right to ordain and consecrate, like degraded bishops, though they keep that of baptizing; that sacraments celebrated by heretics in the Church's form are valid, those in another form void; that they are valid in themselves but void in effect for unworthy givers and receivers; and that only those ordained within the Church keep the right when separated.
claims: The doctors disagree on whether heretics can confer orders.
Some authorities call heretical ordinations and sacrifices void and sacrilegious.
Augustine holds that ordination, like baptism, remains and is not repeated.
Several resolutions distinguish condemned from uncondemned heretics, form, and effect.
Sacraments may be valid in themselves yet void in effect for the unworthy.
